moduleTitle: Jesus: the incarnate Son of God

note.specFocus: The doctrine of the incarnation and its significance for Christian belief about Jesus.
note.sourcePages: Written to match the Edexcel specification; no supplied booklet for this subject.
note.summary:
1.1 Jesus: The Incarnate Son of God
The incarnation is the belief that God the Son became fully human in Jesus Christ while remaining fully divine — "the Word became flesh and dwelt among us" (John 1:14).
Key beliefs
• The virgin birth: Luke 1:26–35 describes Jesus being conceived by the Holy Spirit and born to Mary, showing he was divine from the very start of his human life.
• Fully God and fully human: the Nicene Creed states Jesus is "true God from true God", while Hebrews 4:15 stresses he was tempted "as we are, yet without sin", meaning he can fully understand human experience.
Why the incarnation matters
• It demonstrates the depth of God's love: John 3:16, "God so loved the world that he gave his only Son."
• It underpins Christian belief in salvation: Jesus' death is understood as an atoning sacrifice that could only reconcile humanity with God because he was both truly human (representing humanity) and truly divine (with the power to defeat sin and death).
• It gives Christians a model of how to live — Jesus' life and teaching provide a direct example of God's character expressed in human form.
Exam link: keep the incarnation (Jesus becoming human) distinct from the resurrection (Jesus rising from death) — they are different, though connected, beliefs, and questions may ask about either specifically.

questions.examTip: Make two separate points and develop each one. Link the development directly to the question.
questions.modelAnswer:
A strong response develops two separate points:

1. The incarnation is the belief that God the Son became fully human in Jesus Christ while remaining fully divine, summarised in John 1:14, "the Word became flesh and dwelt among us".

2. Christians believe the virgin birth, in which Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born to Mary (Luke 1:26–35), shows that Jesus was uniquely both divine and human from the very beginning of his life.
questions.question: Outline two beliefs about Jesus as the incarnate Son of God.

questions.examTip: For 6 marks, combine accurate knowledge with explanation. Explain why each point matters and link it directly to the question; avoid simply listing facts.
questions.modelAnswer:
A developed answer could explain the issue through three connected points.

First, The incarnation shows that God chose to enter human history and experience human life directly in Jesus, which Christians believe demonstrates the depth of God's love for humanity, as summarised in John 3:16, "God so loved the world that he gave his only Son".

Second, Because Jesus is believed to be fully human, Christians see him as able to fully understand human suffering and temptation (Hebrews 4:15), while because he is fully God, his teaching, death and resurrection carry divine authority and saving power.

Finally, The incarnation underpins the Christian doctrine of salvation: Jesus' death on the cross is understood as an atoning sacrifice that could only fully reconcile humanity with God because Jesus was both truly human, able to represent humanity, and truly divine, able to overcome sin and death.
questions.question: Explain why the incarnation is important for Christians.

questions.examTip: For a 10-mark discussion, analyse different aspects of the Christian issue and how they interrelate. Finish with a reasoned conclusion; do not just list advantages and disadvantages.
questions.modelAnswer:
A FIRST PERSPECTIVE

One line of reasoning is: St Paul states in 1 Corinthians 15:14 that "if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith is in vain", suggesting the resurrection is the foundation on which all other Christian belief depends.

A second consideration is: The resurrection is celebrated as the most important festival in the Christian calendar, Easter, and is treated as the guarantee of eternal life for believers, giving hope in the face of death.

AN ALTERNATIVE PERSPECTIVE

A different perspective is: Some would argue the incarnation is equally fundamental, since without God becoming human in Jesus there would be no resurrection to speak of; others point to Jesus' teaching and example of self-giving love, especially his death on the cross, as what most directly shapes Christian moral life day to day.

A further consideration is: The crucifixion itself is sometimes highlighted as central because it demonstrates the extent of God's love and the atonement for sin, which some argue is the belief most directly relevant to how Christians understand forgiveness.

JUDGEMENT

Overall, the conclusion should weigh the arguments above against this key consideration: incarnation, crucifixion and resurrection are closely interconnected beliefs, and different Christians and denominations place slightly different weight on each depending on whether they emphasise God's love, atonement, or hope for eternal life. It should then state which perspective is more convincing in relation to the exact wording of the question and explain why, rather than assuming that every Christian will reach the same view.
questions.question: Discuss whether the resurrection is the most important belief about Jesus for Christians.

questions.examTip: Use accurate Christian teaching, explain why each point matters, and in an evaluation compare arguments before reaching a reasoned conclusion.
questions.modelAnswer:
A FIRST PERSPECTIVE
Teaching gives coherent meaning to the themes of Incarnation, fully God and fully human, Word made flesh, revelation and salvation and helps Christians decide what is true.

AN ALTERNATIVE PERSPECTIVE
Practice makes belief visible in worship, compassion, family and service; without action faith may be empty. Christians within different traditions may also disagree about how the teaching should be lived.

JUDGEMENT
A reasoned conclusion should compare the authority and practical effect of belief and action, acknowledge diversity, and decide which is more persuasive for the exact claim.
questions.question:
“Christian teaching about Jesus as the incarnate Son of God is more important than Christian practice connected with it.”
Evaluate this statement, referring to Christianity.

questions.modelAnswer: A developed answer states two separate effects. One concerns belief or worship; the other concerns an ethical choice, practice or sense of community. Each is linked to Incarnation, fully God and fully human, Word made flesh, revelation and salvation.
